extracted.intended_audience: instructors and researchers in undergraduate mathematics education (especially those interested in inquiry-based instruction)
extracted.subtask_description: A categorized bibliography of references and resources for instructors and researchers about inquiry-oriented undergraduate mathematics teaching, instructional change, student thinking, and related topics. The page groups references by topical roles to help instructors find relevant literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overview: grouped resource list for instructors
rubrics_metrics.description: Here we provide a list of references that can be used as resources for instructors; they are grouped by role of the instructor / teaching, instructional change, student thinking, mathematics, and general.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This page functions as a curated bibliography organized by topic to help instructors locate literature relevant to inquiry-oriented undergraduate mathematics education. Use the topical groupings to find readings tailored to instructor role, instructional change, student thinking, mathematical content, social justice connections, and general resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inquiry Based Mathematics Education
rubrics_metrics.description: References focused on inquiry approaches in undergraduate mathematics (e.g., Laursen, S. & Rasmussen, C. (2019). I on the prize: Inquiry approaches in undergraduate mathematics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes research and overviews that articulate inquiry-oriented approaches and frameworks for undergraduate mathematics. Representative citation: International Journal of Research in Undergraduate Mathematics Education, 5(1), 129–146.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of the Instructor / Teaching
rubrics_metrics.description: Works addressing teachers' mathematical activity, teacher listening, implementing inquiry-oriented curriculum, inquiry and gender inequity, conceptualizations of instructional components and practices, and measures for inquiry-oriented instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes empirical and conceptual studies about instructors' roles in inquiry-oriented classrooms, e.g., Johnson (2013) on teachers' mathematical activity; Kuster et al. (2019) on the Inquiry-Oriented Instructional Measure; Rasmussen & Marrongelle (2006) on pedagogical content tools. Useful for instructors reflecting on practice and for research on teaching behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructional Change
rubrics_metrics.description: Literature about changing instruction—eliciting pedagogical reasoning, faculty collaboration (including online working groups), using video for collaboration, and knowledge needed for analytic scaffolding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes conference proceedings and journal articles documenting how mathematicians and instructors change instructional practices, examples of online faculty development, and studies about knowledge needed to support classroom discussions (e.g., Andrews-Larson et al. 2016; Fortune & Keene 2017/2019/2021; Speer & Wagner 2009).

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Thinking
rubrics_metrics.description: Research on students' procedural and conceptual understanding, dynamic reasoning, use of gestures and representations, retention of knowledge, and symbolizing/brokering in inquiry-oriented settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes studies and case analyses focusing on how students reason and learn in inquiry-oriented classrooms (e.g., Bouhjar et al. 2018 on eigenvectors/eigenvalues; Keene 2007 on dynamic reasoning; Rasmussen 2001 on students' understandings and difficulties). Useful for designing instruction centered on student thinking and assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics (content-focused inquiry work)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications that apply inquiry-oriented approaches to specific mathematical content and modeling tasks (e.g., reinventing the Salty Tank, modeling to develop new ideas, using theorems-as-tools).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These works show how inquiry pedagogy interacts with particular mathematical topics (differential equations, linear algebra, modeling), providing concrete classroom cases and pedagogical examples (e.g., Oremland et al. 2021; Rasmussen & Keynes 2003; Rasmussen & Ruan 2008).

rubrics_metrics.name: Social Justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Resources connecting differential equations and other undergraduate math topics to social justice and environmental concerns, such as climate change problems used to explore identity, power, access, and achievement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes special-issue articles and classroom problem examples that integrate social justice themes into mathematics courses (e.g., Dunmyre et al. 2019; Fortune et al. 2020). Useful for instructors seeking to contextualize content in societal issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: General
rubrics_metrics.description: Miscellaneous resources about inquiry-oriented instruction, software tools, teaching ordinary differential equations, advancing mathematical activity, and reflective lessons for teaching practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This category contains broader or cross-cutting resources such as blog posts, magazine pieces, and book chapters (e.g., Johnson et al. 2015 'Inquiry-oriented instruction: What it is and how we are trying to help'; Rota 1997 'Ten lessons I wish I had learned before I started teaching differential equations'). Useful for general background and teaching tips.
